To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
price and brand endorsement have a positive influence on brand impression and brand loyalty, and brand impression partially mediates the relationship between price and endorsement, and brand loyalty.

manufacturer brands support high price premiums and boost those vivid brand impressions which are helpful for engendering consumer brand loyalty, while retail store brands follow distinct price policies and carry out endorsement strategies.
manufacturer brands and retail brands adopt different pricing strategies, and manufacturer brands and retail stores adopt different endorsement strategies.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the impact of price and endorsement strategies adopted by firms from the viewpoint of consumer based brand equity and brand loyalty.
the effects of manufacturer brands' and retail store brands' price/endorsement strategies on consumer brand loyalty.
the brand management of both manufacturer and retailer brands, and offers some useful suggestions on the brand management of manufacturer and retailer brands.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the manufacturer retailer brand co-branding strategy should be used for those products that have the highest price premiums.
the price/endorsement strategy is a powerful tool for brand management.
manufacturer brands and retail brands have their own unique price and endorsement strategies that influence consumer loyalty intention.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the manufacturer brand and retail brand should be viewed as complementary brands.
manufacturers should consider the price and endorsement strategy in a brand portfolio management perspective, and retailers should consider the price premium strategy in a store image perspective.
the price and endorsement strategies of manufacturer and retailer brands are interdependent and complementary, and should be jointly considered in brand management decisions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
manufacturer retailers could benefit from a co branding strategy by leveraging the brand equity of manufacturer brands.
manufacturers should be cautious about the endorsement of a brand, and retailers should not blindly endorse brands without a careful evaluation process.
the effects of price/endorsement strategies on consumer loyalty intention are contingent upon the brand type.
